requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the hazards you are most likely to encounter while using leatherwork tools and materials, and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, or lessen these hazards. (b) Show that you know first aid for injuries or illnesses that could occur while working with leather, including minor cuts and scratches, puncture wounds, ingested poisoning, and reactions from exposure to chemicals such as dyes, cements, and finishes used in leatherworking.

pamphlet_excerpts: Tools Leatherworking Sharp: Many tools used in leatherworking have sharp cutting edges.
Neverput Part Body: Neverput any part of your body in the path of a cutting edge.
Pieceof Cardboard Rubbed: A pieceof cardboard rubbed with jeweler’s rouge should be used forhoning the swivel and utility knife blades.
Dyes Cements Finishes: Many dyes, cements, and finishes used in leatherworkingcontain hazardous chemicals.
step_by_step_procedure: Work Well-ventilated Area: To safely use these materials, work in a well-ventilated area.
Carefully Read Follow: Carefully read and follow alllabel instructions and warnings.
Ingest Chemicalsor Allow: Never ingest these chemicalsor allow them to come in contact with skin.
Doctor Oremergency Medical: Have a doctor oremergency medical service telephone number handy in case ofan emergency.

options: Review the Leatherwork hazards, PPE, and prerequisite standards in Official Scouting America Leatherwork Merit Badge Pamphlet (p. 10, p. 11) with your counselor and patrol buddy before beginning
Begin the practical station immediately and review the safety rules only if a problem occurs
Rely on another patrol's notes instead of inspecting your own equipment and workspace
Skip the pre-activity briefing when practicing indoors
quiz_item.correct_answer: Option A - Review the Leatherwork hazards, PPE, and prerequisite standards in Official Scouting America Leatherwork Merit Badge Pamphlet (p. 10, p. 11) with your counselor and patrol buddy before beginning

pamphlet_excerpts: Types Leather Kinds: Types and Uses of Leather Many kinds of leather are available for leatherwork.
Instance Wayleather Tanned: For instance, the wayleather has been tanned can determine how it is used.
Vegetable Tanned Leather: Vegetable tanned leather (leather that has been tanned with extracts from tree bark) normally is used for items thatcall for a stiff, firm leather.
Chrome Tanned Leather: Chrome tanned leather (leather that has been tanned with chemicals that contain chromium salts) normally is usedfor items that call for a soft.
step_by_step_procedure: Leather Purchased Complete: Leather can be purchased in complete hides or skins.
Oneof Common Leathers: Oneof the more common leathers, cowhide, normally is sold inhalf-skins, called sides.
Common Types Leather: Common types of leather and their usesare listed here to help you select a leather for a project.
Buffalo Common Buffalo: Buffalo, The most common buffalo leather is Asian waterbuffalo.

pamphlet_excerpts: Measuring Pattern Design: Use these for measuring, pattern and design layout, and for cutting straight lines.
Avoid Unpainted Steel: Avoid unpainted steel rulers and squares because they will stainleather; ones made of aluminum, plastic, or wood work best.
Marking Theoutlines Cutting: Use for marking theoutlines of cutting patterns andto mark the positions of holes forsnaps, rivets, stitching, and lacing.
Awl Sharp Point: Any awl with a sharp point, evenan ice pick, will work.
step_by_step_procedure: Utility Knife Box: A utility knife or box knifeworks well for general leatherwork.
Usingsnap-off Blades Ensure: Usingsnap-off blades will ensure a sharp cuttingedge.
Craft Knife Hobby: A craft knife or hobby knife works wellfor projects using lighter-weight leather.
Leather Shearswork Cutting: Leather shearswork well for cutting soft garment leathers but do notproduce as accurate a cut as a sharp knife.

Hiking Boots Backpacks: Hiking boots, backpacks, and manyother products can be made from either leather or synthetic materials likenylon, plastic, vinyl, or rubber.
step_by_step_procedure: Here Few Points: Here are a few points to consider.
Solid Vinyl Material: A solid vinyl material will repel water from the outside but ittraps heat on the inside, making you uncomfortable in warm weather.

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Learn about the commercial tanning process. Report about it to your counselor. (b) Tan the skin of a small animal. Describe the safety precautions you will take and the tanning method that you used. (c) Recondition or show that you can take proper care of your shoes, a baseball glove, a saddle, furniture, or other articles of leather. Discuss with your counselor the advantages or disadvantages of leather vs. synthetic materials. (d) Visit a leather-related business. This could be a leathercraft supply company, a tannery, a leather goods or shoe factory, or a saddle shop. Report on your visit to your counselor.

pamphlet_excerpts: Optional Requirement: An optional requirement for the Leatherwork merit badge isto visit and report on a leather-related business.
Almost Everytown America: Almost everytown in America has a leather-related business available totour.
Small Custom-leather Shop: Whether it’s a small, custom-leather shop or a large industry (tannery, apparel manufacturer, etc.), it will be exciting toexplore the endless ways.
Surprised Welcome: You may be surprised how welcome you will be in theseindustries.
step_by_step_procedure: Shop Factory Managers: Most shop or factory managers will be pleased togive you the “grand tour” and answer questions about their operation.
Overall Understanding: Try to get an overall understanding of exactly whattakes place; take notes and pictures (but ask first, please).
Leather Hand-tooled: Is the leather hand-tooled, machineembossed, sewn, or laced? 4.
Theysold Directly General: Are theysold directly to the general public orto other businesses? 5.
